title: Graphs and data analysis; Estimation and orders of magnitude
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS03-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MS03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS03-1#N.15, MS04-1#N.3, MS04-1#N.6, MS04-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Order of magnitude
items.clue: The nearest power of ten to a value.

items.label: y-intercept
items.clue: Value on the vertical axis where x = 0.

items.label: Tangent
items.clue: Drawn on a curve when its slope at one place is needed.

items.label: Gradient
items.clue: Δy divided by Δx, taken from a large triangle; it has its own units.

questions.stem: A best-fit line has gradient 2.50. The steepest line through all the error bars has gradient 2.65 (same units). What is the percentage uncertainty in the gradient?
Kinetic energy = ½ × mass × speed². What is the order of magnitude of the kinetic energy of an adult walking?
questions.explanation: ½ × 70 kg × (1.5 m s⁻¹)² ≈ 80 J, nearest power of ten 10² J.

questions.stem: What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).

questions.stem: A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.
